q: In which state of matter does diffusion happen fastest?
options: It happens at the same rate in all three states
explain: Gas particles move fastest and furthest between collisions, so gases diffuse quickest.

q: Which statement describes the particles in a gas?
options: They are far apart, in a regular pattern and vibrate about fixed positions.
They are close together, randomly arranged and move quickly in all directions.
They are far apart, randomly arranged and move quickly in all directions.
They are far apart, randomly arranged and vibrate about fixed positions.
explain: Gas particles have large separations, no pattern and fast random motion in all directions.

q: The relative molecular masses of four gases are CH₄ = 16, NH₃ = 17, HCl = 36.5 and Cl₂ = 71. Which list shows the order of rate of diffusion from fastest to slowest?
explain: The lower the relative molecular mass, the faster the diffusion, so the order of rate follows increasing Mr.

q: A diagram shows particles touching each other in neat rows and columns. Which state of matter does it show?
options: A mixture of liquid and gas
explain: Touching particles in a regular pattern are a solid.

q: On a heating curve, the horizontal section for boiling is much longer than the one for melting. Why?
options: There are more particles in the sample when it boils.
The temperature rises faster during boiling.
Boiling releases energy that slows down the heating.
More energy is needed to completely separate the particles when boiling than to free them from fixed positions when melting.
explain: During boiling the attractions between particles are completely overcome, which needs far more energy than loosening them in melting.

q: A sealed syringe contains air. The plunger is pushed in slowly and the temperature stays the same. What happens to the volume and the pressure of the air?
options: The volume decreases and the pressure decreases.
The volume increases and the pressure increases.
The volume and the pressure stay the same.
The volume decreases and the pressure increases.
explain: Squeezing the same amount of gas into a smaller space makes the pressure rise.

q: A gas in a cylinder with a movable piston is heated at constant external pressure. Which explanation of the increase in volume is correct?
options: The forces of attraction between the particles increase.
The particles move faster and hit the piston harder, so the gas expands until the pressure matches the external pressure.
explain: Faster particles push the piston out, and the gas expands until the collisions per unit area fall back to match the external pressure.

q: Hydrogen has Mr = 2 and oxygen has Mr = 32. Which row correctly compares their diffusion at the same temperature?
explain: Hydrogen diffuses faster because its relative molecular mass is lower.

q: Which list contains only changes of state in which the substance gains energy?
explain: Melting, boiling and evaporating all need an energy input. Freezing and condensing release energy.

q: Which gas diffuses fastest at the same temperature and pressure?
explain: Helium has the smallest relative mass (Ar = 4, compared with Mr = 16, 28 and 44 for the others), so it diffuses fastest.

q: A diagram shows a few particles that are widely spaced and not touching. Which state of matter does it show?
options: A mixture of solid and liquid
explain: Widely spaced particles that do not touch are a gas.

q: Why can a liquid evaporate below its boiling point?
options: All the particles in the liquid have enough energy to escape.
Some particles at the surface have enough energy to escape from the liquid.
The covalent bonds in the molecules break.
The pressure at the surface is zero.
explain: Particles in a liquid have a range of energies, so a few at the surface have enough energy to overcome the attractions and leave.

q: Ethanoic acid melts at 17 °C and boils at 118 °C. In which state is it at 10 °C?
options: A mixture of solid and gas
explain: 10 °C is below the melting point of 17 °C, so the substance is solid.

q: Which statement about temperature is correct?
options: It is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles.
It is a measure of the number of particles.
It is a measure of the mass of the particles.
It is a measure of the size of the particles.
explain: A higher temperature means that the particles have a higher average kinetic energy.

q: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride are placed at opposite ends of a tube. They take several minutes to meet in the tube, although the particles move very fast. Why?
options: The particles are too heavy to move.
The particles collide with air particles, which change their direction.
The particles only move when the tube is shaken.
explain: Many collisions with the air in the tube make the movement of each particle a random zigzag, so the net progress is slow.

q: What is the name of the change of state from solid to liquid?
explain: A solid turns into a liquid by melting. Freezing is the reverse change.

q: Which gas diffuses fastest at the same temperature and pressure?
explain: Neon has the smallest relative mass of the four gases, so it diffuses fastest.

q: Which gas diffuses most slowly at the same temperature and pressure?
explain: HCl has the largest relative molecular mass (Mr = 36.5, compared with 17, 16 and 28), so it diffuses slowest.

q: Which statement about a solid is correct?
options: It has a fixed shape but its volume changes to fill its container.
It has a fixed shape and a fixed volume.
It has no fixed shape but it has a fixed volume.
It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume.
explain: The particles in a solid are held in fixed positions, so both its shape and its volume are fixed.

q: In which situation does diffusion take place?
options: A fan blows smoke across a room.
A spoon stirs sugar into tea.
A pump moves water through a pipe.
The smell of cooking spreads through a house with no draughts.
explain: In the others the movement is caused by a fan, a spoon or a pump. Diffusion happens because of random particle motion alone.

q: Nitrogen melts at −210 °C and boils at −196 °C. In which state is nitrogen at −150 °C?
options: A mixture of liquid and solid
explain: −150 °C is above the boiling point of −196 °C, so nitrogen is a gas.

q: Which explanation of the properties of a liquid is correct?
options: The forces between particles hold them in fixed positions, so the shape is fixed.
The forces between particles are negligible, so the liquid fills its container.
The forces between particles keep them close, so the volume is fixed, but they are too weak to hold the particles in fixed positions, so the shape changes.
The particles are far apart, so the liquid can be compressed easily.
explain: Moderate attractions in a liquid keep particles touching but allow them to move past one another.

q: The heating curve of a pure solid has two horizontal sections. What is happening in the first horizontal section?
explain: The first flat section is at the melting point, where solid and liquid are present together. The second flat section is boiling.

q: Which change of state occurs when energy is removed from a liquid?
explain: Taking energy away from a liquid makes its particles move more slowly until they are held in fixed positions, which is freezing.

q: Why can a liquid flow?
options: Its particles can slide past one another.
Its particles are held in a regular lattice.
Its particles are far apart and move freely.
Its particles only vibrate about fixed positions.
explain: Liquid particles are close together but not held in fixed positions, so they can move past each other.

q: Which observation is an example of diffusion in a liquid?
options: Bubbles rise to the surface of a fizzy drink.
A puddle gets smaller on a sunny day.
An ice cube floats in a glass of water.
A purple crystal is placed in still water and the purple colour gradually spreads through the water.
explain: The purple particles from the crystal spread through the water by random motion.

q:
The temperature of a pure substance is recorded as it is heated at a steady rate.
0–2 minutes: rises from −20 °C to 0 °C
2–6 minutes: stays at 0 °C
6–14 minutes: rises from 0 °C to 100 °C
14–26 minutes: stays at 100 °C
What is present after 4 minutes?
explain: The temperature is constant at 0 °C between 2 and 6 minutes, which is the melting point, so solid and liquid are both present.

q: Why can a gas be compressed but a solid cannot?
options: Gas particles are much smaller than solid particles.
Solid particles move too fast to be pushed together.
Gas particles are far apart with much empty space, but solid particles are already touching.
explain: Compression reduces the spaces between particles. There is a lot of space in a gas but almost none in a solid.

q:
Four substances have these melting points and boiling points.
P: −219 °C and −188 °C
Q: −7 °C and 59 °C
R: 801 °C and 1413 °C
S: 0 °C and 100 °C
Which substance is a gas at 25 °C?
explain: Only P has a boiling point below 25 °C, so only P is a gas at 25 °C. Q and S are liquids, and R is a solid.

q: A hot gas is cooled steadily and its temperature is recorded. The cooling curve has a horizontal section at 78 °C. Which change of state is happening in this section?
explain: A flat section on a cooling curve at a substance's boiling point (the same temperature as for condensing) shows the gas changing to liquid.
